{{Short description|British mathematician and selenographer}}
{{Use dmy dates|date=April 2022}}
'''Samuel Arthur Saunder''' (1852 – 8 December 1912) was a British [[mathematician]] and [[selenography|selenographer]] who taught at [[Wellington College, Berkshire]]. In 1894 he became a [[fellow]] of the [[Royal Astronomical Society]], and in 1908 he was made [[Gresham Professor of Astronomy]] giving public lectures on the subject.<ref>{{citation|title=Mr. S. A. Saunder|journal=[[Nature (journal)|Nature]]|volume=90|issue=2250|date=December 12, 1912|pages=415–416|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=KI9FAAAAYAAJ&pg=PA415|doi=10.1038/090415a0|bibcode=1912Natur..90..415.|doi-access=free}}.</ref>

Saunder was one of the first to use [[photography]] of the [[Moon]] to measure and [[Triangulation|triangulate]] its features.<ref>{{citation|title=Planetary Mapping|volume=6|series=Cambridge Planetary Science|editor1-first=Ronald|editor1-last=Greeley|editor2-first=Raymond M.|editor2-last=Batson|publisher=[[Cambridge University Press]]|date=2007|isbn=9780521033732|contribution=Geodetic control|first=M. E.|last=Davies|pages=141–168}}. See in particular [https://books.google.com/books?id=ztodv66A1VsC&pg=PA143 p.&nbsp;143].</ref> He was also responsible for pointing out the confused state of lunar nomenclature at the beginning of the 20th century, and initiating the process of standardizing the names of lunar features.<ref>{{citation|title=Mapping and Naming the Moon: A History of Lunar Cartography and Nomenclature|first=Ewen A.|last=Whitaker|publisher=Cambridge University Press|date=2003|isbn=9780521544146|page=153|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=aV1i27jDYL8C&pg=PA153}}.</ref> The crater [[Saunder (crater)|Saunder]] on the Moon was named after him in 1935.<ref>{{citation|title=The Solar System and the Constellations: A Guidebook|first=Clifford N.|last=Anderson|publisher=[[Vantage Press]]|date=1964|quote=A large ring to the west [sic] of Hipparchus, named for an English selenographer Samuel A. Saunder (1852-1912)}}.</ref><ref>[https://planetarynames.wr.usgs.gov/Feature/5342 Saunder], Gazetteer of Planetary Nomenclature, [[USGS]], retrieved 2014-11-13.</ref>
